## Implementation completed in this pass

The local Cloudflare integration now contains 10 files, including the new edge-side Worker and the replay-recovery tests.

| Requirement | Verified status |
|---|---|
| Recover failed enqueue attempts | Implemented in source |
| Retry interrupted pending claims | Implemented with expiring SQLite leases |
| Prevent duplicate accepted claims | Implemented in source |
| Preserve native queue ownership | Uses `BonfyreQueue enqueue --if-absent` |
| Cloudflare Cron-to-Queue consumer | Worker source added |
| Signed edge-to-native delivery | Worker and ingress source added |
| Retry toward a dead-letter queue | Consumer logic added; queue configuration pending |
| JavaScript syntax checks | Passed after correcting an edge Worker syntax error |
| Repository diff checks | Passed |
| Behavioral test execution | Not yet verified |
| Live Cloudflare deployment | Not yet verified |

The new Cloudflare Worker keeps a stable occurrence identity when retrying delayed work, but refreshes the short-lived transport timestamp. This allows a delayed queue message to be authenticated without creating a different work identity.

### What remains blocked

I confirmed that the connected native command interface can inspect compiled executables, but it does not expose arbitrary Bun test execution. The existing test runner interface also doesn't provide a Bun behavioral-test profile. I have therefore not claimed the new replay tests passed.

The exact behavioral suite to run in the Mac checkout is:

```bash
bun test \
  integrations/cloudflare/workgraph-envelope.test.mjs \
  integrations/cloudflare/workgraph-admission.test.mjs \
  integrations/cloudflare/native-ingress.test.mjs \
  integrations/cloudflare/replay-recovery.test.mjs
```

I also have not provisioned a Cloudflare Queue, attached a dead-letter queue, deployed the Worker, or established the private ingress route. Existing credentials and provider reachability are promising, but they do not prove authorization for those new resources.

**The next execution boundary is clear:** run the native behavioral suite, verify the existing Cloudflare credential owner and account scopes, then deploy through the established Cloudflare deployment owner and exercise enqueue → claim → acknowledgment → retry and recovery.

The manually recovered hard wins should feed the four engineering waves, especially Matrix Crate reuse, objective-to-chain resolution, Creator performance propagation, and the existing native WorkGraph checkpoint system. I have not changed their authoritative implementations or resumed the paused operator. <MemoryCite />

## Backfill findings from the recent sessions

I reviewed the October 12–15 Bonfÿre/Aurekai history and checked the relevant native owners against the current architecture atlas. Several substantial wins were missing from the orchestration plan.

| Existing hard win | What should be reused |
|---|---|
| **Matrix Crate and JSON retirement** | Virtual/delta-only CrateViews, shared representations, and the existing materialize/virtual/verify compiler modes. Preserve JSON only where interoperability requires it. |
| **Creator performance improvements** | Measured 7.43× viewport preparation improvement, 99.74% smaller plans, and 99.2% fewer repeated candidates. Carry the optimizations into native execution. |
| **Capability discovery** | A registry covering 177 native capabilities, with corrections to stale advertisements and executable-owner matching. Use this to resolve objectives into actual execution chains. |
| **WorkGraph transactional checkpoints** | Revision-checked checkpoints, stale-review refusal, transactional completion, family routing, and durable native work ownership. |
| **30-program experience planner** | Native economic verification, dependency planning, and ExperienceStage-to-Queue review handoffs, instead of rebuilding a generic task planner. |
| **ForeignTwin and civic media** | Source imports, clip handoffs, and Dallas council reconciliation that can feed the existing CMS, media, and Creator workflows. |
| **ServiceSite production flows** | Tested catalogue editing, training publication, source-backed document review, receipt recovery, and Cloudflare Pages intake. |
| **Cloudflare provider integration** | Existing provider verification, credential boundaries, PlacementPlane, Pages publishing, R2 material delivery, and no-Worker routing rules. |

One particularly important correction: the native ProviderGraph records earlier successful credentialed reachability checks for **Cloudflare Queues, Workflows, Pages, Workers, and KV**. The previous conclusion that Bonfÿre had no usable Cloudflare capability was too broad. Those credentials still need a fresh readback before provisioning.

The highest-leverage integration target is the existing WorkGraph, BonfyreQueue, CredentialBoundary, and PlacementPlane. The new edge transport must remain subordinate to them.

The 7 AM Cloudflare Edge Federation and 7 PM Execution Recovery schedules are already configured to continue this work. I have not resumed the globally paused operator or modified the held release boundary.
